headline: AIS count 2 ships crossed today, 7-day average 7.1/day (~8% of normal)
dek: On Nov 9, 2026, 2 AIS-visible commercial ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz (2 inbound into the Gulf, 0 outbound; 1 tanker), as of 06:59 UTC. The 7-day average is 7.1 transits a day, about 8% of normal (baseline 84.8/day pre-crisis).
fault_line: Open or closed? CENTCOM says 400 ships a week; the satellites count 7 a day -- who is counting honestly?

sections.what_happened: On Nov 9, 2026, 2 AIS-visible commercial ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz (2 inbound into the Gulf, 0 outbound; 1 tanker), as of 06:59 UTC. The 7-day average is 7.1 transits a day, about 8% of normal (baseline 84.8/day pre-crisis). Status: Restricted (severely restricted), in this status since Oct 19, 2026. Ships cross under US naval coordination; Iran claims control and requires transit permits. IMF PortWatch was re-pulled this scan (2026-11-09) and is STILL stale: latest observation Nov 1, 8-day lag, stale=true -- no counted PortWatch figure is cited as current.
sections.what_verified: 0 declared-tier families. hormuz.now has NO declared tier in ~/workspace/times-dashboard/data/source-registry.md and therefore cannot count toward corroboration. PortWatch (IMF, primary data) is stale and cited only as stale.
sections.what_disputed: CENTCOM claims ~400 merchant ships sailed through in 7 days (Adm. Brad Cooper, Oct 17) and 900M+ barrels assisted since May (Capt. Tim Hawkins, Sept 16 -- that Sept statement was recirculated today via a mirror re-dated Nov 9 05:23Z; it is NOT new, see triage). hormuz.now itself notes counts are AIS-visible only and miss ships running dark. The gap between CENTCOM's ~57/day and the AIS 7.1/day is the core dispute and is unresolved.
sections.why_matters: Two counts, one strait: the US says 400 ships a week, the satellites count 7 a day -- the number that decides whether Hormuz is open.

The fault line our audience is arguing over: Open or closed? CENTCOM says 400 ships a week; the satellites count 7 a day -- who is counting honestly?
